mem.7:
Caroline (surname unknown) and Melanie/Mel (surname unknown) are friends/supportive conversational partners. Caroline is transgender, began transitioning around 2020, and moved from her home country around 2019. Melanie is married with children (including two younger children), a dog and a cat. Melanie and her husband had been married five years as of June 2023 (since about 2018). They encourage each other; Melanie is proud of Caroline’s advocacy and wants to keep motivating and helping her. Caroline is grateful for friends, family and mentors’ support and wants to pass it on, share her experiences, build a hopeful community, and lift others up.

May 8, 2023 — Caroline had attended an LGBTQ support group; hearing trans people’s stories helped her feel accepted and more courageous about embracing herself. She was considering further education and counseling/mental-health work to help people with similar experiences. Mel thought her empathy would make her a good counselor. Caroline shared a photo of a dog by a wall mural of a woman; Mel shared her 2022 painting of a sunrise over a lake, which she valued as a way to express feelings, be creative and unwind. Mel went swimming with her kids; Caroline went to do research.

May 25, 2023 — Mel had run a mental-health charity race on May 20 and was trying to make daily time for self-care (running, reading, violin); family was considering June camping. Caroline was researching adoption agencies, choosing one supportive of LGBTQ+ adopters. Having a family and giving children in need a loving home had long been her dream. She felt hopeful/optimistic, while realizing the hard work of making the dream real was beginning; she knew single parenting could be challenging. She was grateful for support from friends and mentors. Mel said she would be an excellent, caring mother.

June 9, 2023 — Caroline spoke at a school event about her trans journey, coming out and personal growth, encouraging students to engage with the LGBTQ community and be allies. She felt empowered and glad the audience related; she believes sharing stories promotes understanding, acceptance and hope. Friends/family/mentors are her “rocks”; she had known her support network four years, since moving around 2019, and they helped especially after a difficult breakup. Mel said her husband and children motivate and support her. Mel shared family photos: husband and daughter at a waterfall; her wedding photo; family picnic (games, good food, togetherness). Caroline’s necklaces/photo: her Swedish grandmother gave her a cross-and-heart necklace when she was young, symbolizing love, faith, strength and family roots. A friend made her a hand-painted bowl for her 18th birthday (about 2013).

Around June 20, 2023 — Mel’s family camped in the mountains, hiking, exploring, roasting marshmallows; her two younger children love nature and she treasured the summit view and family memories. June 23 — Caroline attended an LGBTQ+ counseling workshop on therapeutic methods and working with trans people. Her own counseling/support groups helped greatly; she hoped to create a safe, welcoming place for others. She was exploring counseling/mental-health work, perhaps supporting trans people. Both shared bookshelf photos.

July 3, 2023 — Caroline attended a pride parade the previous week; belonging and community growth strengthened her desire to help. She planned to attend a transgender conference in July. Mel began pottery; she said it was therapeutic and expressive, and was proud of a black-and-white flower-design bowl she made. Caroline was learning piano. July 5 — Mel took her kids to a museum; they loved the dinosaur exhibit and water-play area. Caroline was making a library for future children, with classics, multicultural stories and educational books. Mel’s favorite childhood book was *Charlotte’s Web*, for friendship and compassion. Caroline shared a picnic photo with her women friends, whose unconditional love, guidance and acceptance were instrumental in her transition. Mel shared a family beach-camping photo by a campfire.

July 10, 2023 — Caroline attended an LGBTQ conference two days earlier. She felt welcomed and accepted, connected with people with similar journeys, and was grateful for the community; she wanted to fight for trans rights, spread awareness and make a difference. She continued exploring counseling/mental-health jobs because support had helped her through mental-health struggles and she wanted others to have support systems. Mel encouraged her and shared a book-cover photo (gold coin); Caroline said books guide and motivate her. Her favorite was *Becoming Nicole* by Amy Ellis Nutt, a true story about a trans girl and her family; it gave her connection and hope and taught self-acceptance, seeking support, and that hard times pass. A dog-in-boat photo was also shared. Mel’s dog and cat appeared in photos; their names are Luna and Oliver, and they bring joy and comfort. Mel shared photos of new pink/purple running shoes; she had been running farther to destress, clear her mind and improve her mental health, and intended to continue.
mem.13:
Caroline (surname unknown) and Melanie (“Mel”; surname unknown) are close, supportive friends. Caroline is transgender, began transitioning around 2020, and moved from her home country around 2019. Mel is married (about 2018) with three children, a dog named Luna, and cats Oliver and Bailey. Mel admires Caroline’s courage, advocacy and transition, and wants to encourage her. Both treasure family and loved ones; Mel feels happy and alive with family, and Caroline says family is everything.

- **May 8:** Caroline attended an LGBTQ support group; hearing others’ stories helped her feel accepted and courageous. She considered education/counseling work; Mel thought she’d make a good counselor. Caroline shared a dog-by-mural photo; Mel shared a sunrise-over-lake painting made in 2022. Mel swam with her kids; Caroline went to do research.
- **May 20–25:** Mel ran a mental-health charity race and tried to make time for self-care (running, reading, violin). Her family considered June camping. Caroline researched LGBTQ-friendly adoption agencies. Having a family and giving children a loving home was a long-held dream; she felt hopeful and optimistic, while knowing the hard work was beginning and single parenting could be challenging. Mel said Caroline would be an excellent mother. Caroline was grateful for friends’ and mentors’ support.
- **June 9:** Caroline spoke at a school about coming out, her trans journey and personal growth, encouraging allyship. Mel said her husband and children motivate her; she shared photos of husband and daughter at a waterfall, their wedding, and family picnic. Caroline’s cross-and-heart necklace from her Swedish grandmother symbolizes love, faith, strength and family roots. A friend made Caroline a hand-painted bowl for her 18th birthday (about 2013).
- **Around June 20:** Mel’s family camped in the mountains, hiked and roasted marshmallows; her two younger children love nature.
- **June 23:** Caroline attended an LGBTQ counseling workshop. Counseling/support groups had helped her, and she hoped to create a safe, welcoming place. They shared bookshelf photos.
- **June 26–July 2:** Caroline attended a Pride parade, felt belonging and was inspired by the LGBTQ+ community’s happiness and growth. She planned to attend a transgender conference in July. On July 2 Mel signed up for pottery; she finds it therapeutic and a way to express herself creatively.
- **July 5–6:** Mel took her children to a museum; they loved the dinosaur exhibit, animal learning and bones, and water play. The outing reminded her why she loves being a mother. Caroline is building a library for future children, including classic children’s books, stories from different cultures and educational books; she looks forward to reading to them and opening their minds. On July 6 Caroline said she was exploring counseling/mental-health work because helping people and making a positive impact matters to her; it is tough but rewarding. Mel’s favorite childhood book is *Charlotte’s Web*. Caroline shared a picnic photo with women friends who supported her transition; Mel shared a family beach-camping photo.
- **July 8–10:** Caroline attended an LGBTQ conference, felt welcomed and wanted to advocate for trans rights. She explored counseling work, inspired by support she received during mental-health struggles. Her favorite book is *Becoming Nicole* by Amy Ellis Nutt; it gave hope and lessons in self-acceptance and seeking support. Mel shared a gold-coin book-cover photo, dog-in-boat photo and pink/purple running shoes; running helps her destress.
- **July 14–15:** Mel took her kids to a pottery workshop; they made pots, clay sculptures and a dog-face cup. They painted a palm-tree sunset and found purple flowers. Caroline attended an adoption council meeting, strengthening her resolve. Mel shared a blue vase with sunflowers and roses. Blue is Caroline’s favorite color (relaxing); she associates sunflowers with warmth/happiness and roses with love/beauty. Mel says flowers mean joy, growth and appreciating small moments; wedding flowers remind her of marrying her husband and promising forever. Caroline’s parade photos showed flags, sign-holders and a dog; she felt proud, accepted and free. Mel shared Buddha/candle and family forest-camping photos.
- **July 17:** Caroline joined an LGBTQ youth mentorship program and mentors a transgender teen; seeing the mentee respond to support was a highlight. They had attended a Pride event together the previous month. Caroline planned an August LGBTQ art show and shared a tree-and-sun painting made after visiting an LGBTQ center, symbolizing unity and strength. Mel shared a blue-and-yellow painting made with her kids and enjoyed a quiet weekend with them.
- **July 18–20:** Caroline joined “Connected LGBTQ Activists,” which meets, plans campaigns/events and supports members. She missed a city parade the previous weekend (separate from parades she attended). Mel’s three kids played with a kite at the beach; family goes once or twice yearly. Camping tradition includes marshmallows and stories. Mel’s favorite memory was watching the Perseid meteor shower the previous year and making wishes; she also cherishes her youngest child’s first steps. Photos included beach/campfire/footprints, sandcastle, starry sky with plane, baby in crib with blue blanket and family at beach sunset.
- **August 13–14:** Mel celebrated her daughter’s birthday at a Matt Patterson concert; she loved the music and seeing her children happy. Caroline called an advocacy event a great experience and said she attended a Pride parade the previous Friday; its energy, love and support renewed her commitment to equality. Photos showed a welcoming band, diverse parade crowd with balloons, and concert audience. Caroline says inclusive representation and LGBTQ advocacy matter in her art. Her paintings express her trans experience and help others understand trans people. “Embracing Identity” depicts a woman journeying toward acceptance, warmth, love and self-acceptance. Art helps Caroline explore transition and her changing body, process experiences and appreciate beauty in imperfection. Mel praised art as healing.
- **August 17:** Caroline recounted a distressing hike encounter with religious conservatives whose remarks upset her and reminded her how much work remains for LGBTQ rights. Acceptance and support help her know she’ll be okay; Mel sympathized. Mel shared a colorful patterned bowl she made, proud of vivid colors/patterns chosen to catch the eye and make people smile. Painting lets her express feelings and creativity; art is a connection, learning experience, sanctuary and comfort. They expressed appreciation for their friendship. Caroline shared a photo of a group with balloons at a Pride fest they attended together the previous year. They discussed a summer family outing and a special nature outing just the two of them; Mel would think of ideas.
- **August 23:** Caroline applied to adoption agencies—the first step toward motherhood—after attending an adoption advice/assistance group. She felt excited but nervous about parenting’s responsibility. She has a guinea pig, Oscar; shared a photo of him eating parsley (his favorite) and said she has always loved horses, recalling childhood rides through fields with her dad. Mel said she had recently added cat Bailey; Oliver once hid his bone in her slipper. Mel shared an Oliver photo (described, though image was a black dog with frisbee) and a photo of feeding a horse a carrot, plus her horse painting on a wooden wall; she enjoys painting animals. Caroline shared a recent blue-faced self-portrait, painted the previous week; she felt liberated and empowered, and finds painting therapeutic for exploring identity and being true to herself. She says freedom also comes from supportive people, LGBTQ advocacy and living authentically; she wants to help others do likewise. Mel congratulated her and offered ongoing support.
